back: A database in which data is held in tables that are linked by matching key values.
A field (or fields) whose value is different in every record, so it identifies one record. It can never be empty.
A field in one table that holds the primary key value of a record in another table; it links the tables.
Candidate key: any field that could be the primary key. Secondary key: a candidate key not chosen as the primary key.
Record (tuple) = a row, all the data about one item. Field (attribute) = a column, one kind of data.
Data redundancy, data inconsistency, program-data dependence, poor sharing, weak security and integrity.
In a one-to-many relationship, in the table on the many side. It holds the primary key of the one side.
Every foreign key value must match an existing primary key value, so there are no orphan records.
A sorted structure on a field that makes searches faster but uses extra storage and slows updates.
